text.p: Australian retail giant Coles Myer Ltd said on Monday it planned to add five new "category-killer" departments to its chain of Myer department stores within the next twelve months.

Coles Myer chief executive Dennis Eck told reporters after a luncheon address that the group planned to roll out Myer Sport, Myer Electric and three others within Myer department stores in Victoria and New South Wales.
Eck said the cost of the new category-killing departments would be minimised by having them in-store.
He said the "category-killer" departments could not be compared to the unsuccessful World-4-Kids chain of separate department stores for toys.
"This is the antithesis of World-4-Kids," Eck told reporters.
Coles Myer had already set up the Myer Sport store within its Melbourne Myer store and aimed to set up its Myer Electric store soon.
Eck said he could not say what the other three "category-killers" were.

Eck said there was the potential to set up the stores separately from the department store, but they would be built from the department store base and would not be built from the groun up as seperate operations.
"We could take it as a lift and take it somewhere else," he said.
"They will see the light of day through the department stores, but they're designed the same way, they're actually stores within those stores," he said.
Coles Myer shares were six cents higher at A$6.34 at 3.15 p.m. (0515 GMT) on Monday.
